title: Three Growth Paths
equation: Growth Capacity = Available Capital × Control Preference × Risk Tolerance
hook: Every dollar you use to grow comes with strings. You just get to pick which ones.
statement: You can fund growth with profits, outside capital, or employee ownership. Each one changes your control, risk, and upside.
explainer: Profits keep you in charge but can be slow. Investors speed things up but take a piece of your future. Employee ownership shares the upside with your team. Know what you're trading.
sop: Estimate how much capital your growth actually needs.
Decide how much control you want to keep.
Compare self-funding, outside money, and employee ownership.
Score Available Capital, Control Preference, and Risk Tolerance from 1 to 10.
Pick the path that fits your long-term vision.
equation_example: Available Capital 4, Control Preference 9, Risk Tolerance 3. 4 × 9 × 3 = 108 Growth Capacity, out of 1,000. Higher means you've got real options for funding growth. Lower means one path, usually the slowest, is your only realistic one.
question: Write down which growth path fits you best right now, and what you'd be giving up to take it.
closing_statement: Every funding choice trades away something else.
caption:
Principle Nº 255: Three Growth Paths

Every dollar you use to grow comes with strings. You just get to pick which ones.

You can fund growth with profits, outside capital, or employee ownership. Each one changes your control, risk, and upside.

Your turn: Write down which growth path fits you best right now, and what you'd be giving up to take it.
